newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat and settlers talk, US criticises Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Arafat and settlers talk, US criticises Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli settlers from two of the most militant Jewish communities in the West Bank have had a meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, according to a PLO official.

The official, who refused to be named, said he attended the meeting on Tuesday, the day that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made his first official visit to a Jewish settlement in the West Bank.
The participants included Jewish residents of Hebron and the Kiryat Arba settlement, he said.

Arafat has met Israeli settlers before, but such meetings are very rare. The Palestinian leader is still regarded by many right-wing Israelis as a terrorist even though he became Israel's partner in a breakthrough 1993 peace deal.

The United States meanwhile delivered its sharpest attack yet on Netanyahu's West Bank settlements policy, which has reversed a building freeze imposed by the previous government, and called the prime minister's show of defiance on the issue unhelpful.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, in an unsolicited statement to reporters in Washington, said: "If you're asking about Prime Minister Netanyahu's visit to the Ariel settlement... I would say that it's a very complicating factor.

"If you look at the potential impact on the peace negotiations, this move today of calling for an expansion of settlements, going to Ariel, is certainly not useful and not constructive. It's not going to help that process."
Netanyahu made his high-profile visit to the entrenched settler community of Ariel just one day after the Palestinian Authority called for an immediate halt to settlement activity.
Defending new building, he asked: "Why not develop communities here?"
The Palestinian official said the meeting between Arafat and the settlers discussed Hebron, the only West Bank town with a Jewish population.
Israel was to have withdrawn its troops from most of Hebron earlier this year but froze the pullout in response to a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in the Jewish state.
Jewish settlers have led the campaign to block Israel's withdrawal from parts of Hebron, where 400 Jews live among 100,000 Palestinians.
Another PLO official who attended the meeting said about a dozen Jewish settlers took part in the talks in the West Bank city of Bethlehem.
He said the settlers expressed readiness to accept Palestinian self-rule and sought peaceful coexistence with Arabs in the West Bank.
But he said he did not think they represented the views of all Hebron settlers.
The self-rule Palestinian Authority did not confirm that the meeting took place and the head of the Jewish local council in Kiryat Arba said he knew nothing about it.
